$comment: Which coding agent a spoken task asks for. Omi lets a user name an agent out loud ('use codex to fix this'), and each desktop platform extracts that name with its own copy of one literal alias table: macOS `desktop/macos/agent/src/runtime/agent-mention.ts`, Windows `desktop/windows/src/main/codingAgent/agentMention.ts`. Two copies of a string-matching rule is exactly the divergence this directory exists to prevent — a negator scoping fix or a new alias applied on one platform and not the other silently changes which agent runs a user's task. Matching is word-boundary and case-insensitive, so 'hermeneutics' is not Hermes. Negation is scoped to the clause containing the mention (boundaries: , ; : . ! ? em/en dash, newline, and the word 'but'), looking back at most 4 words, so 'don't use codex, use hermes' rules out only codex. 'instead' negates rather than ending a clause, because 'use hermes instead of codex' rules codex out. An agent both ruled out and asked for counts as asked for. `expected_agent` is the first non-negated mention, or null when nobody was named; `expected_ruled_out` is the set of agents excluded, order-insensitive.
